title: Web3 Product Discovery & Cold Start Guide
subtitle: Master finding new opportunities and launching successful Web3 products

intro.title: Introduction to Web3 Product Discovery
intro.content:
In the fast-moving Web3 space, being early is everything. The difference between discovering a protocol at testnet versus after mainnet launch can mean the difference between a 100x airdrop and nothing. Similarly, for builders, nailing your cold start strategy can determine whether your product gains traction or dies in obscurity.

This comprehensive guide covers both sides of the opportunity equation: discovering new products early (for users and investors) and launching products successfully (for builders). You'll learn where to find alpha, how to evaluate opportunities, strategies for maximizing airdrop rewards, and proven cold start tactics for Web3 launches.

Why product discovery matters in Web3:

  • Retroactive Airdrops: Early users of Uniswap, dYdX, Arbitrum, and Optimism received $1,000-$50,000+ in airdrops
  • Early Access: First users get better terms, exclusive features, and community status
  • Investment Alpha: Finding projects before they explode can generate life-changing returns
  • Network Effects: Being early means building relationships with founding teams

discovery_channels.title: Discovery Channels: Where to Find New Projects
discovery_channels.content: Web3 moves at lightning speed. New protocols launch daily, and the best opportunities are often discovered before they hit mainstream attention. Here's where to hunt for alpha.

product_hunt.title: Product Hunt: Tech Product Discovery
product_hunt.content:
Product Hunt is where new tech products launch to the world. While not Web3-specific, many crypto projects use it for initial exposure.

How to Use Product Hunt for Web3:

  • Filter by "Blockchain" and "Cryptocurrency" categories
  • Check daily launches every morning (products launch at midnight PT)
  • Look for makers with crypto backgrounds in their profiles
  • Early upvotes can get you on the founding team's radar

What to Look For:

  • Products in pre-launch or beta phase (waitlist opportunities)
  • Tools that solve real Web3 problems (not just hype)
  • Teams with verifiable backgrounds (check LinkedIn links)
  • Comments from recognizable Web3 builders

Pro Tips:

  • Enable email notifications for specific topics
  • Follow prolific Web3 makers and hunters
  • Engage early—makers remember and reward early supporters
  • Many projects offer early access codes to active Product Hunt users

Example Success: Rainbow Wallet launched on Product Hunt in 2020 before mobile wallet explosion. Early users who provided feedback got direct access to the team and early feature access.

twitter_alpha.title: Twitter/X: The Alpha Hunter's Paradise
twitter_alpha.content:
Twitter (X) is the primary communication channel for Web3. Alpha leaks here first, often weeks before official announcements.

Who to Follow:

  • VCs: Paradigm, a16z crypto, Dragonfly—they tweet about portfolio companies before public launch
  • Builders: Follow protocol founders, they share testnets and beta access
  • Alpha Callers: Accounts that specialize in finding airdrops and early opportunities
  • Researchers: Delphi Digital, Messari analysts drop research on emerging sectors

Search Strategies:

  • Search "testnet" + "incentivized" daily
  • Monitor "waitlist" + "early access" for beta opportunities
  • Track "raising" + "seed round" for newly funded projects
  • Follow hashtags: #airdrop #testnet #Web3

Advanced Techniques:

  • Create Twitter Lists for different categories (VCs, builders, alpha accounts)
  • Use TweetDeck/Hootsuite for real-time monitoring
  • Set up notifications for key accounts (ring bell icon)
  • Join Twitter Spaces hosted by projects—ask questions, get noticed

Red Flags:

  • Accounts promising "guaranteed" airdrops (scams)
  • New accounts with generic names promoting "hot opportunities"
  • Accounts asking for seed phrases or private keys
  • Too-good-to-be-true returns promised

Case Study: Arbitrum Airdrop
Hints dropped on Twitter months before the official announcement. Users who followed Arbitrum team members saw hints about "rewarding early users" and positioned themselves by using the network actively. Result: $1,000-$10,000+ per address.

communities.title: Discord & Telegram: Inside the Community
communities.content:
Discord and Telegram are where Web3 communities live. This is where you get direct access to teams and insider information.

Discord Strategies:

  • Join Early: Many projects reward OG Discord members with special roles and airdrops
  • Be Active: Participate in discussions, not just lurking. Active members get whitelisted
  • Watch Announcements: Enable notifications for #announcements channels
  • Testnet Channels: Check #testnet or #developers channels for early access links
  • AMAs: Attend Ask-Me-Anything sessions to understand team thinking

What to Look For:

  • Active development discussions (good sign)
  • Transparent team communication
  • Community helping each other (healthy community)
  • Regular updates and milestone progress

Telegram Tips:

  • Join official announcement channels (read-only, less noise)
  • Participate in community discussion groups
  • Many projects use Telegram for testnet coordination
  • Watch for scam bots—admins never DM first

Ambassador & Moderator Programs:
Many projects recruit community ambassadors who get:

  • Early access to features
  • Direct communication with core team
  • Token allocations or increased airdrop multipliers
  • Governance roles

Application Tips:

  • Demonstrate genuine interest in the project
  • Show previous contributions (articles, tweets, translations)
  • Highlight relevant skills (design, community management, development)
  • Be patient—good projects are selective

Warning: Never share private keys or seed phrases in Discord/Telegram. Legitimate projects never ask for these. Always verify URLs before clicking—scammers create fake channels.

data_platforms.title: Data Platforms: On-Chain Discovery
data_platforms.content:
Data platforms help you discover trending protocols before they hit mainstream radar by tracking on-chain metrics.

DeFiLlama: The essential DeFi analytics platform

  • Recently Listed: Check the newest protocols added (potential airdrops)
  • Trending: Fast-growing TVL often indicates product-market fit
  • New Chains: Early protocols on new chains often airdrop heavily
  • Fork Scanner: Find new forks of successful protocols

How to Use:

  1. Visit DeFiLlama daily, check "Recently Listed Protocols"
  2. Filter by chain (new L2s often have airdrop opportunities)
  3. Look for protocols with growing TVL but no token yet
  4. Check if team is doxxed and reputable
  5. Visit the protocol, start using it early

DappRadar: Discover trending dApps across all chains

  • Filter by "New Dapps" to find fresh launches
  • Track user growth—early movers often get rewarded
  • Multi-chain coverage (not just EVM)
  • NFT and gaming discovery

CoinMarketCap/CoinGecko: Track new token listings

  • Recently Added: New tokens just listed
  • Trending: What's gaining attention
  • Categories: Filter by sector (AI, DeFi, Gaming)
  • ICO/IEO Calendar: Upcoming token sales

Advanced Platform: Nansen
Premium tool ($100+/month) for serious alpha hunters:

  • Smart Money Tracking: See what wallets of successful investors are buying
  • Token God Mode: Deep analytics on any token
  • Wallet Labels: Identify VCs, founders, and whales
  • Early Signals: Detect tokens before they pump

Free Alternatives:

  • Etherscan: Track new contract deployments
  • DeBank: Wallet tracking and protocol discovery
  • Dune Analytics: Community dashboards highlighting new protocols

early_access.title: Early Access Strategies: Get In Before the Crowd
early_access.content: Early access to Web3 products can mean the difference between massive airdrops and nothing. Here's how to systematically position yourself as an early user.

beta_testing.title: Beta Testing Programs
beta_testing.content:
Why Projects Need Beta Testers:

  • Find bugs before mainnet launch
  • Get user feedback on UX/features
  • Build early community and advocates
  • Generate social proof and testimonials

How to Get Beta Access:

  1. Sign Up Early: Join waitlists the moment you discover a project
  2. Show Expertise: Mention relevant experience in applications
  3. Be Active on Socials: Teams check if you're an engaged community member
  4. Provide Value: Offer to write docs, create tutorials, or translate
  5. Network: Connect with team members on Twitter/LinkedIn

Maximizing Beta Participation:

  • Give Quality Feedback: Don't just use the product—report bugs, suggest features
  • Document Everything: Take screenshots, record sessions (with permission)
  • Create Content: Write threads, tutorials—teams love this
  • Be Patient: Beta programs can last months, stay engaged

What You Can Earn:

  • Airdrop Allocations: Many projects reward beta testers (Optimism, Arbitrum did this)
  • NFT Badges: Proof of early participation, sometimes valuable
  • Whitelist Spots: Priority access for token sales or NFT mints
  • Direct Tokens: Some projects pay testers directly
  • Reputation: Build track record as quality tester

Example: Coinbase Wallet Beta
Early testers of Coinbase Wallet's Web3 features received exclusive NFTs, early access to new features, and direct communication with product team.

Where to Find Beta Programs:

  • Project Discord #announcements channels
  • Twitter announcements (search "beta testers wanted")
  • Product Hunt "Coming Soon" pages
  • Layer3, Galxe, QuestN platforms (often host beta quests)

testnet_participation.title: Testnet Participation: The Airdrop Meta
testnet_participation.content:
Testnet participation has become the most reliable airdrop farming strategy. Projects launching new chains or major protocols often reward testnet users.

Why Testnets Lead to Airdrops:

  • Helps projects stress-test infrastructure
  • Builds early user base familiar with the product
  • Creates community before mainnet launch
  • Demonstrates commitment from users

Major Testnet Airdrops:

  • Optimism: Testnet users received 3-5x multipliers on airdrop allocation
  • Arbitrum: Users who bridged and transacted on testnet got higher allocations
  • zkSync: Testnet activity heavily weighted in eligibility criteria
  • Aptos: Active testnet validators and users received significant allocations

How to Participate Effectively:

  1. Get Testnet Tokens: Use faucets to get free test ETH/tokens
  2. Perform Diverse Actions: Don't just bridge—swap, provide liquidity, deploy contracts
  3. Be Consistent: Transact regularly over weeks/months, not just once
  4. Use Multiple Features: If it's a DEX, also try lending, staking, governance
  5. Engage Authentically: Projects can detect bots and farmers

    6. Testnet Best Practices:

    • Separate Wallets: Use different wallets for different testnets (organize tracking)
    • Document Activity: Keep record of transactions (some projects ask for proof)
    • Report Bugs: File issues on GitHub—shows genuine participation
    • Join Testnet Discord: Get support, hear about new features to test

    Finding Active Testnets:

    • Follow "testnet" hashtag on Twitter
    • Check Layer3, Galxe for testnet campaigns
    • Monitor ecosystem Discord servers (Ethereum, Cosmos, Solana)
    • Visit project documentation—often lists testnet details

    Time Investment:

    • Initial setup: 30-60 minutes per testnet
    • Ongoing: 10-20 minutes weekly for transactions
    • Potential return: $500-$10,000+ per successful airdrop

    Red Flags:

    • Testnet asking for mainnet funds (never happens)
    • Promising guaranteed airdrops (never guaranteed)
    • Asking for KYC during testnet phase (unusual)
    • Unknown projects with no real team or backers

ambassador_programs.title: Ambassador Programs: Earn While You Build
ambassador_programs.content:
Ambassador programs turn engaged community members into project advocates, offering rewards, early access, and influence.

What Ambassadors Do:

  • Create educational content (threads, tutorials, videos)
  • Answer community questions in Discord/Telegram
  • Organize local meetups or online events
  • Translate documentation and announcements
  • Test new features and provide feedback
  • Represent the project at conferences

What You Get:

  • Token Allocations: Monthly stipends or large one-time grants
  • Exclusive Access: Try features before public release
  • Direct Communication: Private channels with core team
  • Governance Power: Often given voting rights in DAOs
  • Networking: Connect with other high-level community members
  • Credibility: Boost your Web3 resume

How to Apply:

  1. Build Track Record: Start creating content about the project before applying
  2. Show Up: Be active in community for weeks/months first
  3. Demonstrate Skills: Show writing ability, technical knowledge, or design skills
  4. Propose Value: In application, explain specific ways you'll contribute
  5. Be Genuine: Teams can tell if you're only in it for rewards

Skills That Stand Out:

  • Content Creation: Writing, video editing, graphic design
  • Technical: Development, smart contracts, infrastructure
  • Community: Moderation, event organization
  • Languages: Translation to non-English markets (huge demand)
  • Business Development: Partnership sourcing, strategic outreach

Ambassador Program Examples:

  • Chainlink: Community advocates program—organize events, create content, earn LINK
  • Polygon: Polygon Advocate program—technical content, developer support
  • The Graph: Advocate DAO—decentralized ambassador program with clear contribution levels

Commitment Level:

  • Typical requirement: 10-20 hours/month
  • Duration: Usually 3-6 month terms, renewable
  • Compensation: $200-$2,000+/month depending on program and contribution level

Red Flags:

  • Programs asking you to pay to join (scam)
  • Requiring you to buy tokens before applying
  • Promising specific token amounts upfront (usually performance-based)
  • No clear responsibilities or expectations

product_evaluation.title: Evaluating New Products: Due Diligence Framework
product_evaluation.content: Not every new project is a good opportunity. Most fail. Here's how to separate signal from noise and identify projects worth your time and capital.

team_background.title: Team Assessment: Who's Building This?
team_background.content:
Why Team Matters Most: In early-stage Web3, you're betting on the team's ability to execute. Product, market, and tokenomics can all evolve—team quality is the constant.

What to Research:

  1. Founder Background:
    • Previous companies/projects? Were they successful?
    • Educational background (top schools = easier fundraising)
    • Technical expertise (can they actually build this?)
    • Industry reputation (what do others say about them?)
  2. Team Composition:
    • Is there a technical co-founder/CTO?
    • Do they have relevant Web3 experience?
    • Have they worked together before?
    • Are there gaps in expertise?
  3. Advisors:
    • Are they actively involved or just lending their name?
    • Do they have relevant domain expertise?
    • Have they advised successful projects before?

Where to Research:

  • LinkedIn: Verify employment history, education, connections
  • GitHub: Check code contributions (if technical team)
  • Twitter: See what they tweet about, who follows them
  • Google: Search names for press mentions, controversies
  • Crunchbase: See previous ventures and funding

Green Flags:

  • Founders previously exited successful Web2/Web3 companies
  • Team from top tech companies (Google, Meta, Coinbase, etc.)
  • Core contributors to major open-source projects
  • Multiple team members with 5+ years Web3 experience
  • Active GitHub with substantial code contributions
  • Advisors who are genuinely engaged (attending meetings, tweeting about project)

Red Flags:

  • Anonymous team (unless privacy-focused protocol)
  • Fake LinkedIn profiles or unverifiable backgrounds
  • No technical co-founder on a technical product
  • Previous failed projects not disclosed
  • Advisors who just lent their name for tokens
  • Entire team is first-time founders with no relevant experience

Case Study: Good Team
Uniswap Founder (Hayden Adams):

  • Mechanical engineer, taught himself Solidity
  • Transparent about being first-time founder
  • Built initial version himself (real technical ability)
  • Received Ethereum Foundation grant (community validation)
  • Open-source everything (trust through transparency)

Case Study: Red Flags
Many rug pulls share these characteristics:

  • Team uses stock photos or AI-generated images
  • No verifiable history or LinkedIn profiles
  • Claims to be "ex-Google engineers" with no proof
  • Advisors deny involvement when asked

funding_investors.title: Funding & Investor Analysis
funding_investors.content:
Why Funding Matters: VC-backed projects have runway to build, connections for partnerships, and signals of institutional validation. But not all funding is equal.

Evaluating the Round:

  1. Amount Raised:
    • Too little ($500k): May not have enough to execute
    • Reasonable ($2-10M seed): Enough for 18-24 months
    • Too much ($100M+ seed): Massive dilution for future community
  2. Valuation:
    • Low valuation ($10-50M seed): More room for token appreciation
    • High valuation ($500M+ seed): Tokens may launch overvalued
  3. Round Type:
    • Pre-seed/Seed: Very early, highest risk, highest potential
    • Series A/B: More mature, derisked but less upside
    • Strategic: Industry players investing = validation

Investor Quality Tiers:

Tier 1 (Best Validation):

  • Paradigm, a16z crypto, Dragonfly, Framework Ventures
  • Polychain, Multicoin, Pantera
  • Coinbase Ventures, Binance Labs

Tier 2 (Good Validation):

  • Alameda Research (RIP), Jump Crypto, DeFiance Capital
  • Delphi Digital, Mechanism Capital, 1kx
  • Robot Ventures, Electric Capital

Tier 3 (Some Validation):

  • Smaller focused funds
  • Angels with good track records
  • Regional Web3 funds

What VCs Bring Beyond Capital:

  • Network: Introductions to partners, exchanges, other founders
  • Recruiting: Help hire top talent
  • Strategy: Guidance on tokenomics, go-to-market, governance
  • Credibility: Their reputation validates your project

How to Research Funding:

  • Crunchbase: Track funding rounds
  • The Block: Crypto funding news
  • Project Announcements: Twitter/blog posts
  • VC Websites: Portfolio pages list investments

Red Flags:

  • "Stealth" funding from undisclosed sources
  • Unknown VCs with no track record
  • Funding claims that can't be verified
  • All funding from the team's own wallets (no external validation)
  • Extremely high seed valuations ($1B+) for unproven protocols

Green Flags:

  • Multiple top-tier VCs co-leading (competition = good signal)
  • Strategic investors from the relevant industry
  • Follow-on rounds from existing investors (shows continued belief)
  • Reasonable valuations with room for growth

Note: Some of the best Web3 projects (Uniswap, Yearn) started with minimal or no VC funding. Community-first projects can also succeed—don't discount them just because they lack big-name backers.

tokenomics.title: Tokenomics: The Economic Design
tokenomics.content:
Tokenomics determines whether a token is designed for sustainable value accrual or just a pump-and-dump. Understanding this is critical.

Supply Distribution Analysis:

Healthy Distribution:

  • Community/Ecosystem: 40-60%
  • Team: 10-20% (with 12+ month cliff, 24-48 month vesting)
  • Investors: 15-25% (with 6-12 month cliff, 12-24 month vesting)
  • Treasury: 10-20%
  • Public Sale/Airdrop: 5-15%

Red Flag Distribution:

  • Team + Investors > 50% (insiders control majority)
  • Public allocation < 3% (not enough decentralization)
  • No vesting on team tokens (can dump immediately)
  • Unclear "Other" category > 10%

Token Utility Assessment:

Strong Utility:

  • Governance: Real voting power on meaningful decisions
  • Fee Capture: Token holders earn protocol revenue
  • Staking Rewards: Earn yield for providing security/liquidity
  • Required for Use: Must hold/burn token to use protocol
  • Buyback & Burn: Protocol uses revenue to reduce supply

Weak Utility:

  • Governance with no real power (team overrules community)
  • Staking with unsustainable APYs (Ponzi mechanics)
  • "Discount token" (minor fee reductions)
  • No clear value accrual mechanism

Emission & Inflation:

  • High Inflation (>10%/year): Constant sell pressure, hard to maintain value
  • Moderate Inflation (2-5%/year): Reasonable if matched by growth
  • Low/Zero Inflation: Good for value retention
  • Deflationary: Bullish if burn rate is sustainable

Key Metrics to Calculate:

  1. FDV (Fully Diluted Valuation):
    • Total supply × current price
    • Shows what market cap would be if all tokens were circulating
    • Compare to similar projects at maturity
  2. Circulating Supply %:
    • (Circulating / Total) × 100
    • Low % = huge future dilution
  3. Unlock Schedule:
    • When do large amounts unlock?
    • Expect price drops around major unlocks

Example Analysis:

Project A:

  • Total Supply: 1B tokens
  • Circulating at Launch: 100M (10%)
  • Current Price: $1
  • Market Cap: $100M
  • FDV: $1B (10x current market cap)
  • Assessment: Massive dilution ahead, risky

Project B:

  • Total Supply: 100M tokens
  • Circulating at Launch: 60M (60%)
  • Current Price: $2
  • Market Cap: $120M
  • FDV: $200M (1.67x current market cap)
  • Assessment: Reasonable dilution, more sustainable

roadmap_execution.title: Roadmap & Execution Track Record
roadmap_execution.content:
Anyone can make promises. Execution is what matters. Here's how to evaluate if a team can deliver on their roadmap.

Roadmap Red Flags:

  • Extremely ambitious timelines ("Mainnet in 2 months")
  • Vague milestones ("Q2: Marketing initiatives")
  • No clear prioritization (everything is "high priority")
  • Overpromising features ("We'll replace Ethereum")
  • No technical details (just marketing fluff)

Roadmap Green Flags:

  • Specific, measurable milestones
  • Realistic timelines with buffer
  • Clear phase sequencing (MVP → Beta → V1 → V2)
  • Technical depth in descriptions
  • Past milestones hit on time

Tracking Execution:

  1. GitHub Activity:
    • Are there regular commits?
    • Is development active or has it stalled?
    • Are issues being addressed?
    • How many contributors?
  2. Product Updates:
    • Does team ship new features regularly?
    • Are updates meaningful or just minor tweaks?
    • Do they announce features before building them?
  3. Communication:
    • Regular updates (weekly/bi-weekly)?
    • Transparent about delays and challenges?
    • Team accessible in Discord/Telegram?
  4. Milestone History:
    • Check previous roadmap versions—did they hit targets?
    • Were major features delayed repeatedly?
    • Did scope change significantly?

Development Stage Assessment:

Idea Stage (Highest Risk):

  • Just whitepaper, no code
  • Risk: 90%+ never ship anything
  • Only invest small amounts in exceptional teams

Testnet Stage (High Risk):

  • Working prototype, limited functionality
  • Risk: 50%+ fail to reach sustainable mainnet
  • Good for airdrop farming, cautious on investment

Mainnet Launch (Medium Risk):

  • Live product, early users
  • Risk: Depends on traction and competition
  • Watch for growth metrics

Established Product (Lower Risk):

  • Product-market fit achieved, significant users
  • Risk: Growth may be priced in, less upside
  • Safer for larger allocations

Questions to Ask:

  1. Has the team shipped a working product before?
  2. What's their average time from announcement to delivery?
  3. Do they iterate based on user feedback?
  4. Is development pace accelerating or slowing?
  5. Are they solving real problems or chasing hype?

Example: Execution Excellence
Optimism:

  • Promised retroactive airdrops → Delivered 4 rounds so far
  • Said they'd decentralize governance → Launched OP token and governance
  • Committed to public goods funding → RetroPGF funding rounds executing
  • Result: Community trusts them because they execute on promises

Example: Execution Failure
Many "Ethereum killers" from 2021:

  • Promised better tech, faster speeds, more decentralization
  • Raised massive amounts in public sales
  • Delayed mainnet launches repeatedly
  • Delivered subpar products with low usage
  • Tokens down 90%+ from all-time highs

cold_start.title: Cold Start Guide for Builders
cold_start.content: You've built something amazing. Now the hard part: getting your first users. Here's how Web3 products successfully cold start.

launch_strategies.title: Launch Strategies That Work
launch_strategies.content:
The Cold Start Problem: Products need users to be valuable, but users only join valuable products. How do you break this cycle?

Pre-Launch: Build Anticipation

  1. Waitlist Strategy:
    • Launch waitlist 2-3 months before product
    • Offer tiered access (early supporters get in first)
    • Give waitlist members referral codes (incentivize spreading word)
    • Share metrics publicly ("10,000 people waiting!")
  2. Build in Public:
    • Tweet progress weekly (dev updates, challenges solved)
    • Show screenshots, demos, behind-the-scenes
    • Engage with community feedback
    • Let people feel invested in the journey
  3. Content Marketing:
    • Write about the problem you're solving
    • Share insights from building
    • Guest post on relevant publications
    • Create educational content that attracts your target users

Launch Day: Product Hunt Playbook

  1. Timing:
    • Launch on Tuesday-Thursday (highest traffic)
    • Go live at 12:01 AM PT (full 24 hours of voting)
    • Avoid major holidays or big tech launch days
  2. Preparation:
    • Prepare assets: logo, tagline, first comment, demo video
    • Line up hunter (established Product Hunt user) or self-post
    • Brief your team on response strategy
    • Set up analytics to track traffic spike
  3. Engagement:
    • Respond to every comment within first 2 hours
    • Share on Twitter with compelling thread
    • Post in relevant Discord/Telegram communities
    • Email your waitlist with "We're live!"
  4. First Comment:
    • Introduce yourself and the problem you're solving
    • Offer special deal for Product Hunt users (exclusive access, discount)
    • Ask for specific feedback
    • Include call-to-action

Twitter Launch Strategy

  1. Announcement Thread:
    • Start with the problem (relatable hook)
    • Show what you built (demo video/screenshots)
    • Explain why you built it (your story)
    • Call to action (sign up link)
    • Tag relevant people/projects
    • Ask for retweets
  2. Momentum Building:
    • Quote-tweet with user testimonials
    • Share milestones ("100 users in first hour!")
    • Post behind-the-scenes content
    • Engage with everyone who mentions your product
  3. Influencer Outreach:
    • DM 20-30 relevant accounts before launch
    • Offer early access in exchange for feedback
    • Don't ask for promotion—let them naturally share if they like it
    • Focus on genuine fit, not just follower count

Community Launch (Discord/Telegram)

  • Don't just spam—provide value first
  • Share in communities where your target users are
  • Frame as "I built this for people like us"
  • Offer special perks to community members
  • Be available for questions

Guerrilla Tactics:

  • Answer questions on Reddit/Stack Overflow where your product is relevant
  • Comment on blog posts about related topics
  • Participate in Twitter Spaces on relevant themes
  • Join Discord communities as genuine member, mention product when appropriate

community_building.title: Building Your Initial Community
community_building.content:
Your first 100 users are the most important. They'll provide feedback, spread the word, and shape your product's culture.

Week 1: The Launch Week

  1. Personal Onboarding:
    • Personally message first 50-100 users
    • Ask: What brought them to your product?
    • Invite them to exclusive Discord/Telegram channel
    • Request feedback on their experience
  2. Create Founding Member Benefits:
    • Special Discord role ("OG Member")
    • Exclusive NFT or badge
    • Lifetime discounts or fee reductions
    • Early access to all future features
    • Governance rights in future DAO
  3. Set Up Communication:
    • Discord server or Telegram group
    • Clear channels: #announcements, #general, #support, #feedback
    • Welcome bot with onboarding flow
    • Team members actively participating

Month 1-3: Community Nurturing

  1. Weekly AMAs:
    • Host Ask-Me-Anything sessions
    • Be transparent about challenges
    • Share roadmap and get input
    • Make community feel heard
  2. Feature Request Process:
    • Create public feature voting (Discord polls, Canny, etc.)
    • Implement top requested features fast
    • Publicly credit users who suggested features
    • Show community they influence product direction
  3. Content from Community:
    • Encourage user-generated content
    • Retweet user threads about your product
    • Feature community tutorials in your docs
    • Showcase power users
  4. Early Advocate Program:
    • Identify most engaged users
    • Offer them ambassador roles
    • Give them special responsibilities and perks
    • Turn them into evangelists

Retention Tactics:

  • Regular Updates: Ship new features weekly, communicate progress
  • Recognition: Shout out active members publicly
  • Events: Host community calls, competitions, hackathons
  • Exclusive Access: Give early community special treatment
  • Tokens/Points: Introduce points system for engagement (future airdrop hints)

Discord Server Best Practices:

  • Channel Organization:
    • Keep it simple at first (5-10 channels max)
    • Add more as community grows
    • Clear channel descriptions
  • Moderation:
    • Recruit community moderators early
    • Have clear rules and enforce them
    • Ban scammers immediately
    • Protect your members
  • Bots:
    • MEE6 or Dyno for moderation
    • Welcome bot for new members
    • Leveling system for engagement
    • Useful bots only—don't overdo it

Telegram Best Practices:

  • Separate announcement channel (read-only) and discussion group
  • Pin important messages
  • Use admin bots for auto-moderation
  • Respond quickly—Telegram users expect speed

Converting Community to Users:

  • Don't just build community—drive product usage
  • Share use cases and success stories
  • Create challenges and quests
  • Reward active product users, not just chatters

growth_hacking.title: Web3 Growth Hacking Tactics
growth_hacking.content:
Growth hacking in Web3 combines traditional tactics with crypto-native incentives. Here are strategies that work.

Referral & Viral Mechanics

  1. Referral Programs:
    • Give referrer and referee both rewards
    • Track referrals on-chain or via unique codes
    • Leaderboard for top referrers
    • Example: Blur's aggressive referral system drove massive adoption
  2. Points Systems:
    • Award points for actions (transactions, invites, TVL)
    • Make points tradeable or hint at future token conversion
    • Display leaderboards publicly
    • Example: Friend.tech points drove FOMO and growth
  3. NFT Badges:
    • Award NFTs for milestones (first trade, 100 txns, etc.)
    • Make them display in wallets as status symbols
    • Create rarity tiers (common → legendary)
    • Example: Optimism's attestation NFTs

Airdrop Marketing

  1. Retroactive Airdrop Hints:
    • Never promise airdrop explicitly (regulatory risk)
    • Drop hints: "We believe in rewarding early users"
    • Point to other projects that did retroactive drops
    • Let community speculate and FOMO in
  2. Snapshot Mechanics:
    • Take random snapshots of active users
    • Announce: "We took a snapshot on X date"
    • Creates fear of missing out on future snapshots
    • Drives sustained usage, not just one-time farming
  3. Task-Based Airdrops:
    • Partner with Layer3, Galxe, QuestN
    • Create campaigns with specific tasks
    • Reward completion with NFTs or points
    • Drives targeted actions (add liquidity, make trades, etc.)

Partnership Growth

  1. Protocol Integrations:
    • Integrate with established protocols (list on aggregators)
    • Co-marketing announcements
    • Cross-promote to each other's communities
  2. Liquidity Mining Programs:
    • Offer token rewards for providing liquidity
    • Partner with other protocols for dual rewards
    • Time-limited campaigns to create urgency
  3. Strategic Collaborations:
    • Joint campaigns with complementary products
    • Shared liquidity pools
    • Bundled offerings

Content & SEO

  1. Educational Content:
    • Write guides solving problems in your niche
    • Create comparison content ("X vs Y")
    • Rank for keywords your target users search
  2. Tutorial Videos:
    • YouTube tutorials on using your product
    • Short-form content for Twitter/TikTok
    • Incentivize community to create content
  3. Documentation:
    • Excellent docs = less support burden + better SEO
    • Make docs discoverable (clear, searchable)
    • Translate to multiple languages

Web3-Native Channels

  • DeFi Aggregators: Get listed on 1inch, CowSwap, etc.
  • Analytics Platforms: Get tracked by DeFiLlama, DappRadar
  • Wallet Integrations: Integrate with Rainbow, MetaMask, Rabby
  • DAO Partnerships: Get protocols' DAOs to use your product

Controversial But Effective

  • Vampire Attacks: Incentivize users to migrate from competitors (see SushiSwap vs Uniswap)
  • Aggressive Token Emissions: High APYs to bootstrap liquidity (unsustainable long-term)
  • Airdrops to Competitor Users: Airdrop to users of similar protocols

Metrics to Track:

  • Daily/Monthly Active Users (DAU/MAU)
  • Retention (7-day, 30-day)
  • Viral coefficient (how many users does each user bring?)
  • Cost of acquisition vs lifetime value
  • Time to first action (faster = better)

Warning: Growth hacks can drive vanity metrics without real product-market fit. Don't confuse airdrop farmers with genuine users. Focus on retention and value creation.

airdrop_farming.title: Airdrop Farming: Maximizing Early User Rewards
airdrop_farming.content: Airdrop farming has become a legitimate strategy for earning in Web3. Done right, it can generate significant income. Done wrong, it's a waste of time.

early_user_rewards.title: Understanding Early User Rewards
early_user_rewards.content:
Why Projects Airdrop:

  • User Acquisition: Cheaper than traditional marketing
  • Decentralization: Distribute tokens to actual users, not just investors
  • Community Building: Create aligned stakeholders
  • Regulatory Considerations: Avoid securities classification by distributing broadly

Types of Airdrops:

  1. Retroactive Airdrops:
    • Reward past users without prior announcement
    • Based on historical usage data
    • Cannot be gamed (snapshot already taken)
    • Examples: Uniswap, Optimism, Arbitrum
  2. Prospective Airdrops:
    • Announced before criteria are met
    • Users know what actions will be rewarded
    • Risk of being gamed by mercenary farmers
    • Examples: Many newer protocols with points systems
  3. Hybrid Model:
    • Mix of retroactive + prospective
    • Multiple snapshots over time
    • Rewards both early users and ongoing activity
    • Examples: Optimism's multi-round approach

Largest Airdrops in History:

  • Uniswap (UNI): $1,200-$6,000 per wallet (2020)
  • dYdX: $1,000-$100,000+ based on trading volume (2021)
  • Optimism (OP): $500-$20,000 across multiple rounds (2022-2024)
  • Arbitrum (ARB): $1,000-$10,000+ per wallet (2023)
  • Aptos (APT): $1,000-$5,000 for testnet users (2022)

Common Airdrop Criteria:

  • Number of transactions on the protocol
  • Volume traded or liquidity provided
  • Duration of activity (weeks/months active)
  • Diversity of actions (not just one type of transaction)
  • Testnet participation
  • Discord/community engagement
  • Governance participation (voting)
  • Unique month activity (active in 6+ different months)

What Projects Look For:

  • Genuine Users vs Farmers: Projects try to filter out bots
  • Sustained Activity: Regular usage over time, not just one day
  • Meaningful Transactions: Real capital at risk, not dust amounts
  • Community Engagement: Discord activity, governance votes

points_systems.title: Points Systems: The New Meta
points_systems.content:
Points systems have become the standard way projects reward early users while hinting at future token airdrops.

How Points Systems Work:

  1. Protocol launches without a token
  2. Users earn "points" for actions (TVL, transactions, referrals)
  3. Leaderboards display top point earners
  4. No explicit promise of token airdrop (regulatory gray area)
  5. Eventually, points convert to tokens or determine allocation

Points Earning Strategies:

  • Capital Deployment: Higher TVL = more points per day
  • Consistent Activity: Daily/weekly actions often earn multipliers
  • Referrals: Bring friends, earn % of their points
  • Early Participation: Some systems give multipliers to early users
  • Loyalty: Staying active over months earns bonuses

Example: Blur's Points System

  • Launched NFT marketplace with no token
  • Users earned points for listing NFTs, making bids, holding BLUR NFTs
  • Aggressive referral program (10% of referee's points)
  • Three "seasons" of points before token launch
  • Points converted to BLUR tokens in airdrop
  • Top farmers earned $100,000+ from months of activity

Evaluating Points Systems:

  1. Is Token Likely?
    • VC-backed projects more likely to have tokens
    • Check if team has mentioned tokenomics
    • Look at comparable projects
  2. Dilution Risk:
    • How many people farming points?
    • If millions of farmers, your % will be tiny
    • Early systems = less dilution
  3. Time Commitment:
    • Some systems require daily check-ins (high effort)
  4. Others reward passive capital deployment (low effort)
  5. Calculate effort vs potential return
  6. Capital Requirements:
    • Do you need to deploy meaningful capital?
    • What's the opportunity cost? (Could you earn more elsewhere?)

Red Flags:

  • Points system with no clear product-market fit (why would anyone use this?)
  • Anonymous team (they could rug after collecting TVL)
  • Ponzi-like mechanics (unsustainable rewards)
  • No VC backing (less likely to actually launch token)

Green Flags:

  • Solid product people actually want to use
  • Reputable team and investors
  • Reasonable time horizon (3-12 months, not 2+ years)
  • Clear documentation of point mechanics
  • Fair distribution (not all going to whales)

Managing Multiple Points Farms:

  • Spreadsheet tracking: Protocol, capital deployed, points earned, estimated value
  • Diversify: Don't put all capital in one farm
  • Set alerts for important dates (snapshots, new campaigns)
  • Automate where possible (some protocols allow this)

optimal_strategies.title: Optimal Airdrop Farming Strategies
optimal_strategies.content:
Professional airdrop farmers treat this like a job. Here's how to maximize your edge.

Portfolio Approach:

  • High Conviction (40% of farming capital):
    • 3-5 projects with strong fundamentals
    • VC-backed, real product-market fit
    • Higher capital deployment
  • Medium Conviction (40%):
    • 10-15 projects with decent potential
    • Spread risk across multiple opportunities
    • Moderate capital and time investment
  • Lottery Tickets (20%):
    • 20+ low-effort farms
    • New testnets, simple tasks
    • Minimal capital, just for exposure

Capital Efficiency:

  1. Layer Your Capital:
    • Deploy on lending protocol (earn interest)
    • Use that as collateral to borrow
    • Deploy borrowed funds in another farm
    • Manage liquidation risk carefully
  2. Liquid Staking:
    • Stake ETH for stETH
    • Use stETH in DeFi farms
    • Earn staking rewards + farm points
  3. LP Positions:
    • Provide liquidity on new DEXs
    • Earn trading fees + potential airdrop
    • Watch for impermanent loss

Sybil vs Single Wallet Strategy:

Single Wallet:

  • Pros: Lower transaction costs, easier to manage, some protocols reward bigger users
  • Cons: Caps on per-wallet allocations mean you miss out

Multiple Wallets (Sybil):

  • Pros: Bypass per-wallet caps, diversify risk
  • Cons: Higher gas costs, complex to manage, risk of being filtered
  • Note: Many projects now filter Sybil farmers. Proceed with caution.

Anti-Sybil Tactics Projects Use:

  • Minimum transaction counts or volume
  • Unique monthly activity requirements
  • Time-based criteria (active for 6+ months)
  • On-chain analysis (clustering wallets with similar behavior)
  • Requiring ENS or other identity verification

Smart Farming Tactics:

  1. Be Human:
    • Don't use same amounts across wallets (e.g., exactly 1.00 ETH)
  2. Vary transaction times and types
    • Engage with different features
    • Some wallets do more, some less
  3. Long-Term Activity:
    • Start early, stay active for months
    • Projects reward sustained users over mercenary farmers
    • Sporadic activity over time > one big week
  4. Community Engagement:
    • Join Discord, be active (without spamming)
    • Provide genuine feedback
    • Vote in governance proposals
    • Some projects weight this heavily
  5. Diversify Actions:
    • Don't just bridge—swap, provide liquidity, use dApps
    • Try all features of the protocol
    • Demonstrates genuine usage

Time Management:

  • Active Farms: Daily check-ins, higher potential (1-2 hours/day)
  • Passive Farms: Set and forget, check weekly (15 min/week)
  • Testnet Farms: Front-load effort, then minimal (2 hours initial setup)

Risk Management:

  • Never farm with money you can't afford to lose
  • Use separate wallets from your main holdings
  • Be cautious with unaudited protocols (smart contract risk)
  • Watch for rug pulls—if it seems too good to be true, it is
  • Don't FOMO into every farm—be selective

Tax Considerations:

  • Airdrops are taxable events in most jurisdictions
  • Track cost basis and fair market value at receipt
  • Gas fees are deductible expenses
  • Consult a crypto tax professional

Expected ROI:

  • Good farms: 20-100% APY on capital deployed
  • Great farms: 100-500% (rare)
  • Duds: 0% (many farms won't airdrop at all)
  • Portfolio approach: Aim for 30-50% average across all farms

risk_assessment.title: Risk Assessment: Avoiding Scams and Failures
risk_assessment.content: The Web3 space is filled with scams, rug pulls, and failed projects. Here's how to protect yourself.

rug_pull_signs.title: Recognizing Rug Pull Warning Signs
rug_pull_signs.content:
What is a Rug Pull? When developers abandon a project and run away with investors' or users' funds.

Common Rug Pull Tactics:

  1. Liquidity Drain:
    • Dev provides initial liquidity on DEX
    • Hype builds, people buy
    • Dev removes all liquidity, token becomes worthless
  2. Massive Token Dump:
    • Team holds huge allocation
    • No vesting or lock-up
    • Team dumps on the community
  3. Smart Contract Backdoor:
    • Hidden functions to mint unlimited tokens
    • Pause functionality allowing dev to freeze trading
    • Ownership transfer allowing unilateral control

Pre-Launch Red Flags:

  • ❌ Anonymous team with no track record
  • ❌ Copied whitepaper (plagiarism)
  • ❌ No working product, just promises
  • ❌ Unrealistic promises ("1000x guaranteed")
  • ❌ Pressure to buy ("Limited time!", "FOMO now!")
  • ❌ No audit or audit from unknown firm
  • ❌ Team controls >50% of supply with no vesting
  • ❌ No liquidity lock

Post-Launch Red Flags:

  • ❌ Development stops (no GitHub commits)
  • ❌ Team goes silent
  • ❌ Roadmap milestones repeatedly missed
  • ❌ Liquidity decreasing (dev might be exiting)
  • ❌ Top holders selling heavily
  • ❌ Community concerns ignored

Smart Contract Red Flags:

  • Unverified contract (can't read the code)
  • Mint function (allows creating unlimited tokens)
  • Pause function (dev can stop trading)
  • Ownership not renounced (dev retains control)
  • Extremely high transfer fees (>5%)
  • Blacklist function (can ban addresses from trading)

Social Red Flags:

  • Fake Twitter followers (sudden jumps, low engagement)
  • Stock photos for team members
  • Paid shillers in Telegram/Discord
  • Moderators delete critical questions
  • No real community, just hype men

Famous Rug Pulls:

  • Squid Game Token (SQUID): $3M+ stolen, contract prevented selling
  • AnubisDAO: $60M drained within minutes of launch
  • Meerkat Finance: $31M rug pull on BSC
  • Uranium Finance: $50M stolen from liquidity pools

How to Protect Yourself:

  1. Never invest more than you can lose
  2. Always check if liquidity is locked (Team Finance, Unicrypt)
  3. Read the audit report, don't just see "audited"
  4. Verify team identities (doxxed teams less likely to rug)
  5. Check contract on Etherscan—is it verified?
  6. Use rug checker tools: Token Sniffer, RugDoc
  7. If 3+ red flags, walk away

due_diligence.title: Due Diligence Checklist
due_diligence.content:
Before investing time or money into a project, complete this checklist.

1. Team Research (15-30 min)

  • □ Search each team member on LinkedIn
  • □ Verify employment history is real
  • □ Check GitHub for code contributions (if dev team)
  • □ Google names for controversies or past failures
  • □ Verify advisors actually involved (check their Twitter)

2. Product Evaluation (20-30 min)

  • □ Does a working product exist?
  • □ Have you used it yourself?
  • □ Is there real product-market fit or just hype?
  • □ Check GitHub: Is development active?
  • □ Read the documentation: Is it detailed and clear?

3. Smart Contract Audit (10-15 min)

  • □ Has the contract been audited?
  • □ By whom? (Tier 1: CertiK, Trail of Bits, OpenZeppelin)
  • □ Read the audit report—were critical issues found and fixed?
  • □ Is the contract verified on Etherscan/BSCscan?
  • □ Run through Token Sniffer or RugDoc

4. Tokenomics Review (15-20 min)

  • □ Review token distribution—is it fair?
  • □ Check vesting schedules for team and investors
  • □ Calculate FDV vs market cap ratio
  • □ Is there real token utility or just speculation?
  • □ Check if liquidity is locked

5. Community Assessment (10-15 min)

  • □ Join Discord/Telegram—what's the vibe?
  • □ Ask critical questions—how do mods respond?
  • □ Check Twitter followers—real or bought?
  • □ Read Reddit or forum discussions for unbiased opinions
  • □ Are people genuinely excited or just moonboys?

6. Funding & Investors (10 min)

  • □ Has the project raised funding?
  • □ From whom? (Check investor quality)
  • □ Verify funding claims on Crunchbase or The Block
  • □ Check investors' portfolios—do they have good track records?

7. Competitive Analysis (10 min)

  • □ Who are the competitors?
  • □ What's this project's differentiation?
  • □ Is there a clear moat or is it easily replicated?
  • □ Compare market caps to similar projects

8. Roadmap & Execution (10 min)

  • □ Is the roadmap realistic or overly ambitious?
  • □ Have past milestones been hit on time?
  • □ Is development pace consistent?
  • □ Are there clear deliverables or vague promises?

Total Time: 1.5-2.5 hours per project

Scoring System:

  • 8/8 sections pass: High confidence, suitable for larger investment
  • 6-7 sections pass: Medium confidence, small position acceptable
  • 4-5 sections pass: Low confidence, lottery ticket only
  • Less than 4 pass: Avoid entirely

Tools for Due Diligence:

  • Token Sniffer: Automated scam detection
  • RugDoc: Security reviews and rug checks
  • DexTools: Chart analysis, holder distribution
  • Etherscan/BSCscan: Contract verification
  • Nansen: Wallet analysis (premium)
  • Dune Analytics: On-chain data dashboards

red_flags.title: Comprehensive Red Flags List
red_flags.content:
Team & Project Red Flags:

  • ❌ Fully anonymous team (unless privacy protocol)
  • ❌ Fake or unverifiable team identities
  • ❌ No technical co-founder on technical product
  • ❌ Team with history of failed or scam projects
  • ❌ Advisors who deny involvement
  • ❌ No GitHub activity or private repo only
  • ❌ Whitepaper plagiarized from other projects

Tokenomics Red Flags:

  • ❌ Team + Investors hold >50% of supply
  • ❌ Public sale allocation <3%
  • ❌ No vesting for team tokens
  • ❌ Extremely high FDV compared to market cap (>10x)
  • ❌ Unclear or hidden token distribution
  • ❌ Mint function in smart contract
  • ❌ Pause or blacklist functions
  • ❌ No liquidity lock or very short lock period

Product & Execution Red Flags:

  • ❌ No working product, just ideas
  • ❌ Copied codebase with no innovation
  • ❌ Unrealistic roadmap ("Launch in 2 weeks")
  • ❌ Missing all announced deadlines
  • ❌ Development stops after launch
  • ❌ No real users, only airdrop farmers

Marketing & Community Red Flags:

  • ❌ Guaranteed returns promised ("100x minimum")
  • ❌ Urgency tactics ("Last chance to buy!")
  • ❌ Paid shillers and influencers only
  • ❌ Fake social media followers
  • ❌ Moderators delete critical questions
  • ❌ Community is only hype, no substance
  • ❌ Referral/MLM structure (pyramid scheme)

Security Red Flags:

  • ❌ Unaudited smart contracts
  • ❌ Audit by unknown/sketchy firm
  • ❌ Unverified contract on blockchain explorer
  • ❌ Critical audit issues not addressed
  • ❌ Requests for seed phrases or private keys
  • ❌ Suspicious wallet connection requests

Financial Red Flags:

  • ❌ Unsustainable yields (>1000% APY)
  • ❌ Ponzi-like mechanics (recruit to earn)
  • ❌ No clear revenue model
  • ❌ Funding from unknown or unverifiable sources
  • ❌ No investor backing but claiming to have raised millions

How Many Red Flags Before You Walk?

  • 1-2 red flags: Proceed with caution, small position only
  • 3-4 red flags: High risk, probably avoid
  • 5+ red flags: Definite scam, stay away

Trust Your Gut:

If something feels off, it probably is. The Web3 space has more scams than legitimate projects. When in doubt, sit it out. There's always another opportunity.

discovery_system.title: Building Your Discovery System
discovery_system.content: Successful alpha hunters don't rely on luck—they build systems to consistently discover opportunities early. Here's how.

alerts_setup.title: Setting Up Alerts and Monitoring
alerts_setup.content:
Twitter/X Alerts:

  1. Notifications:
    • Turn on notifications for key accounts (VCs, builders)
    • Create Twitter Lists for different categories
    • Use TweetDeck for real-time monitoring
  2. Keyword Monitoring:
    • Set up searches for: "testnet", "waitlist", "early access", "airdrop", "raising seed"
    • Save these searches and check daily
    • Use tools like TweetDeck to monitor in real-time
  3. Advanced Searches:
    • "testnet" + "incentivized" -filter:retweets
    • "waitlist" + "early access" from:ParadigmEng
    • "announcing" + "seed round" min_faves:100

Discord Monitoring:

  • Enable notifications for #announcements channels only (avoid spam)
  • Join 20-30 high-quality project servers
  • Check announcements daily (morning routine)
  • Watch for testnet launches, beta programs, governance proposals

Telegram Alerts:

  • Join announcement channels (read-only) for projects you track
  • Mute discussion groups (too noisy)
  • Check daily for important updates

On-Chain Monitoring:

  • DeFiLlama: Set up alerts for new protocols added
  • DappRadar: Check "New Dapps" section daily
  • Nansen (Premium): Smart money alerts—see what successful wallets are buying
  • Dune Alerts: Create dashboards tracking metrics, get email alerts

Email Newsletters:

  • Daily: The Block, Bankless, Milk Road
  • Weekly: Week in Ethereum, Messari, Delphi Research
  • Specialized: Subscribe to newsletters from specific ecosystems (Arbitrum, Optimism, etc.)

Google Alerts:

  • Set up alerts for: "[Project Name] testnet", "Web3 seed funding", etc.
  • Frequency: As-it-happens or daily digest
  • Helps catch news you might miss on social media

Calendar & Reminders:

  • Track token unlock dates (sell pressure incoming)
  • Governance proposal deadlines
  • Mainnet launch dates
  • Airdrop claim deadlines

Organization System:

  • Spreadsheet with columns: Project, Stage, Date Discovered, Capital Deployed, Expected Airdrop Date, Notes
  • Update weekly with progress
  • Archive completed airdrops
  • Track success rate and ROI

following_alpha.title: Following Alpha Hunters
following_alpha.content:
Who to Follow for Alpha:

Tier 1 VCs (Early Signals):

  • @paradigm - Paradigm portfolio companies
  • @a16zcrypto - a16z crypto investments
  • @dragonfly_xyz - Dragonfly portfolio
  • @hasufl - Independent researcher, great insights
  • @delvingbitcoin - Bitcoin deep dives

Alpha Callers & Airdrop Hunters:

  • @DeFi_Airdrops - Airdrop opportunities
  • @TheDeFinvestor - Airdrop farming strategies
  • @AirdropAddict - Testnet and airdrop calls
  • @CryptoGirlNova - Early opportunity hunter

Builders & Founders:

  • Follow founders of successful projects
  • They often tweet about new projects they're excited about
  • They share testnet links and early access

Researchers & Analysts:

  • @0xBreadguy - DeFi research
  • @_Checkmatey_ - On-chain analytics
  • @MessariCrypto - Market research
  • @DelpDigital - Deep dives

How to Build Your Follow List:

  1. Start with 20-30 quality accounts
  2. See who they retweet and engage with
  3. Follow people who consistently provide value
  4. Unfollow noise—ruthlessly prune your feed
  5. Create Lists to categorize (VCs, Builders, Researchers, etc.)

Twitter Spaces:

  • Join Spaces hosted by projects you track
  • Ask questions—teams remember active participants
  • Network with other attendees
  • Often where alpha leaks first

Engagement Strategy:

  • Don't just lurk—engage meaningfully
  • Reply with thoughtful comments (not just "Great thread!")
  • Share insights from your own experience
  • Build relationships—Web3 is small, reputation matters

Warning: Filter Out Noise

  • Many "alpha callers" are just promoting their bags
  • Verify everything independently
  • Be skeptical of guaranteed returns
  • Follow process, not hype

curating_sources.title: Curating Your Information Sources
curating_sources.content:
Information Diet: Just like a healthy diet, you need to curate your information sources for quality and relevance.

Tier 1 Sources (Daily Check):

  • Twitter Feed: Curated follow list (20-30 accounts)
  • Discord: Announcements from 5-10 high-priority projects
  • DeFiLlama: Recently listed protocols
  • Email: One daily newsletter (The Block or Bankless)

Tier 2 Sources (Weekly Check):

  • DappRadar: New dApps section
  • GitHub Trending: Crypto repositories
  • Research: Delphi, Messari long-form reports
  • Governance Forums: Major protocols' forums for proposals

Tier 3 Sources (Monthly Check):

  • Ecosystem Reports: Quarterly updates from L2s, ecosystems
  • VC Portfolios: Review what top VCs have invested in
  • Conferences: Watch talks from major conferences

Content Aggregation Tools:

  • Feedly: RSS reader for blogs, newsletters
  • Notion: Create a dashboard with embedded feeds
  • TweetDeck: Multi-column Twitter monitoring
  • Discord Dashboard Bots: Aggregate announcements

Quality Filters:

  1. Source Credibility: Is this person/publication consistently accurate?
  2. Timeliness: Am I getting information early or after everyone knows?
  3. Signal-to-Noise: Is the majority of content valuable or spam?
  4. Bias Check: Is this source shilling their own bags?

Time Management:

  • Morning Routine (30 min):
    • Scan Twitter feed
    • Check Discord announcements
    • Review DeFiLlama new listings
  • Midday (15 min):
    • Quick Twitter check
    • Respond to important threads
  • Evening (30 min):
    • Deep dive into 1-2 interesting projects discovered
    • Update tracking spreadsheet
    • Plan next day's activities

Weekly Review (1 hour):

  • Review your active farms and positions
  • Research new opportunities in depth
  • Exit farms that no longer make sense
  • Update portfolio allocation

Avoid Information Overload:

  • Don't try to follow everything—impossible and stressful
  • Focus on 2-3 ecosystems or niches
  • Take breaks—burnout is real
  • Quality over quantity always

Building a Second Brain:

  • Use Notion, Obsidian, or Roam for note-taking
  • Create templates for evaluating projects
  • Save important threads and articles
  • Build your own knowledge base over time

Community Intelligence:

  • Join small, high-quality alpha groups (paid or exclusive)
  • Contribute value to get value
  • Share findings with trusted peers
  • Collective intelligence > solo hunting

Continuous Improvement:

  • Track which sources led to successful finds
  • Double down on what works
  • Cut sources that waste your time
  • Adapt as the meta changes

cold_start.definition: The initial challenge of launching a product when you have no users. In Web3, successful cold start strategies often involve incentives like airdrops, points systems, and community building to attract the first wave of users.

product_market_fit.definition: The stage where a product satisfies strong market demand. In Web3, this is evidenced by organic growth, high retention rates, and users who would be very disappointed if the product disappeared.

testnet.definition: A blockchain network used for testing and development purposes where tokens have no real value. Many projects reward testnet participants with mainnet airdrops to incentivize stress-testing their infrastructure before launch.

mainnet.definition: The primary blockchain network where real transactions occur and tokens have actual value. Mainnet launch is a major milestone indicating a project is ready for production use.

alpha.definition: Early or exclusive information that gives you an edge. In Web3, alpha refers to discovering opportunities before they become widely known—such as upcoming airdrops, new protocols, or emerging trends.

beta.definition: A pre-release version of a product available to limited users for testing. Beta testers often receive early access benefits, special roles, and airdrop allocations for providing feedback and finding bugs.

airdrop.definition: Free distribution of tokens to wallet addresses, often used to reward early users, build community, and decentralize token ownership. Airdrops can range from $100 to $50,000+ depending on the project and your activity.

retroactive_airdrop.definition: An airdrop announced after the qualifying actions have occurred, rewarding past users without prior knowledge. Examples include Uniswap (2020), Optimism (2022), and Arbitrum (2023), which collectively distributed billions in tokens to early users.

points_system.definition: A gamification mechanism where users earn points for actions like trading volume, liquidity provision, or referrals. Points often hint at future token airdrops, though projects typically avoid explicit promises for regulatory reasons.

waitlist.definition: A pre-launch list of interested users waiting for access to a product. Getting on waitlists early can lead to founding member benefits, beta access, and preferential airdrop allocations.

ambassador.definition: Community members who represent and promote a project in exchange for rewards. Ambassadors typically create content, answer questions, organize events, and receive token allocations, early access, and governance rights.

growth_hacking.definition: Creative, low-cost strategies to grow a user base rapidly. In Web3, this includes referral programs, viral points systems, strategic airdrops, and protocol integrations to bootstrap network effects.

rug_pull.definition: A scam where developers abandon a project and steal investors' funds, often by removing liquidity or dumping pre-allocated tokens. Common in DeFi, rug pulls have stolen billions from unsuspecting users.

due_diligence.definition: The process of thoroughly researching a project before investing time or capital. This includes evaluating the team, reviewing tokenomics, checking smart contract audits, and assessing product-market fit to avoid scams and poor investments.
